title: The Passive with Se at the Mine

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the passive *se* from B1 Unit 6: *se* + a verb that agrees with the noun that follows (*se busca una persona*, *se buscan personas*). It lets you describe a process without saying who does it, which is just what a text about mining needs.

sections.title: Passive se in a mining process
rows: singular noun, singular verb: the rock is crushed
Se construyen plantas desalinizadoras en la costa.
plural noun, plural verb: desalination plants are built
Se exportan los cátodos a muchos países.
the verb agrees with the noun that follows: *cátodos*, so *exportan*
works in the past too: Codelco was created

items.spanish: Primero se rompe la roca con explosivos.
items.english: First the rock is broken with explosives.

items.spanish: Se construyen plantas desalinizadoras en la costa.
items.english: Desalination plants are built on the coast.

items.spanish: Los cátodos de cobre se exportan a muchos países.
items.english: The copper cathodes are exported to many countries.

items.spanish: En 1971 se nacionalizó la gran minería del cobre.
items.english: In 1971 the large-scale copper mining was nationalised.

sections.content: Singular noun, singular verb (*se tritura la roca*); plural noun, plural verb (*se exportan los cátodos*). The noun can come before the verb (*Los cátodos se exportan*) or after it, and the verb still agrees with it.
